stick_economics_the_finance_arithmetic_v.question: Economics - the finance arithmetic, verified and sealed

ticks.claim: [compound interest] $1000 at 5% compounded monthly for 10 years grows to A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) = 1000(1 + 0.05/12)^120 = $1647.01 (sealed through economics.ECON_VERIFY). Interest on interest - the engine of saving and of debt.
[the rule of 72] At 7%, money doubles in about 72/7 = 10.3 years (sealed) - the mental shortcut for the doubling time, accurate to the half-year here.
[present value] $1000 due in 3 years, discounted at 5%, is worth PV = FV/(1+r)^t = $863.84 today (sealed). The time value of money: a dollar later is worth less than a dollar now.
[price elasticity] A 10% fall in quantity against a 5% rise in price is PED = (-10)/(5) = -2.0 (sealed) - demand is elastic: quantity moves more than price.
[GDP per capita] $21 trillion over 331 million people is $63,444 per person (sealed) - the measure divided by the people it is spread across.

[the model it assumes] These are accounting identities and definitions, true by arithmetic. The wider theory (supply and demand, rational actors, ceteris paribus) is a MODEL - it works often enough to reason with, so its conclusions are inferred, never kept as fact; the engine seals the arithmetic and declines the forecast.

[what is declined] Asset valuations, market direction, interest-rate moves, policy outcomes and any forecast are DECLINED, cited or left as a want - not investment advice, and a miss stays a miss. The engine certifies the computation, not the prediction.
